newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas seen continuing rally on open.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas seen continuing rally on open.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open steady to higher Tuesday in continuance of Monday's rally and firmer cash prices, industry sources said.
September over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.58 to $2.59 after settling Monday at $2.586.
On ACCESS, September last traded 0.9 cent higher at $2.595, just one cent shy of the new contract high.
The cash market still clutched onto futures as Henry Hub prices were talked about five cents higher at $2.58-2.62.
Technically, September resistance was first pegged at the high of $2.605, with further selling likely at $2.64-2.655. Support was seen at $2.475, and then around $2.34 and $2.30.
In Monday's cash, Gulf Coast prices rebounded more than 15 cents to about $2.50. Midcon pipes jumped about 20 cents to the mid-$2.40s. New York city gate gas also firmed 20 cents to the low-$2.70s.

Cooler-than-normal weather is expected to cover most of the East and Midwest this week, while heat continues to bake the southern and western parts of the Southwest, according to Weather Services Corp.
Separately, the 610 megawatt Oyster Creek nuclear unit, operated by GPU Nuclear Corp, is expected to restart later today following repairs, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission reported.
Also, injection estimates for Wednesday's storage report are about 75 bcf, traders said.
